summary: Defines a basic set of managed objects for SNMP-based event notification management of DOCSIS-compliant cable modems and cable modem termination systems. It is a standards-track MIB document.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4547 gives cable networks a standard set of alarms to send over SNMP. DOCSIS defines many things that can go wrong, and each belongs to a category. This document creates one notification for each category, one set for the modem at the customer and one for the equipment at the head end. Each notification carries the priority of the event, its number, a short description, and enough device detail to work out which piece of equipment it was.

subtitle: A standard set of SNMP notifications that cable modems and their head-end systems can send when DOCSIS events happen.

tldr.problem: Cable operators were managing thousands of DOCSIS modems a day with SNMP, but only a minimal set of notifications existed, so events on the devices were hard to see.
tldr.mechanism: The MIB module defines one notification object for each DOCSIS event category, in two groups, one for cable modems and one for head-end systems, each carrying the event level, the event id, the event text and device details in its varbinding list.
tldr.outcome: A manager can switch on the categories it cares about and be told when something fails, such as a failed dynamic service request or a software upgrade. RFC 4547 was later updated by RFC 9141.

today: RFC 4547 was published in June 2006 as a Proposed Standard and has since been updated by RFC 9141. The notifications it defines remain the standard way for DOCSIS devices to report events.

sections.title: The Internet-Standard Management Framework
sections.content:
For a detailed overview of the documents that describe the current Internet-Standard Management Framework, the memo points to section 7 of RFC 3410.

Managed objects are accessed via a virtual information store, termed the Management Information Base or MIB. MIB objects are generally accessed through the Simple Network Management Protocol. Objects in the MIB are defined using the mechanisms defined in the Structure of Management Information. This memo specifies a MIB module that is compliant to SMIv2, which is described in RFC 2578, RFC 2579 and RFC 2580.
sections.plainLanguage: A MIB is a named set of counters and settings a device exposes. SNMP reads and writes them, and SMIv2 is the notation this document uses to define them.

sections.title: Glossary
sections.content:
The terms come either from normal cable system usage or from the documents associated with the DOCSIS process.

BPI, the Baseline Privacy Interface, is a mechanism for providing data privacy over the hybrid fiber and coax network in DOCSIS 1.0 systems. BPI+, the Baseline Privacy Plus Interface, extends the Baseline Privacy Interface with the addition of cable modem authentication over that network in DOCSIS 1.1 and 2.0 systems and beyond.

CATV originally meant Community Antenna Television and is now used for any cable or hybrid fiber and cable system used to deliver video signals to a community. A CM, a cable modem, acts as a slave station in a DOCSIS-compliant cable data system. A CMTS, a Cable Modem Termination System, is a generic term covering a cable bridge or cable router in a head-end. It acts as the master station in a DOCSIS-compliant cable data system, is the only station that transmits downstream, and controls the scheduling of upstream transmissions by its associated cable modems.

DOCSIS stands for Data-over-Cable Service Interface Specifications and refers to the ITU-T J.112 Annex B standard for cable modem systems, commonly known as DOCSIS 1.0. DOCSIS 1.1 is an extension of DOCSIS 1.0 with new features to support quality of service, fragmentation, and requirements for European cable plants. DOCSIS 2.0 builds upon DOCSIS 1.1 and provides all of its features, and in addition provides significant enhancements in upstream capacity, such as 30.72 Mbps maximum upstream channel capacity, Synchronous-Code Division Multiple Access operation, increased robustness to upstream noise and channel impairments, Enhanced Reed-Solomon error correction, and Trellis Coded Modulation.

Downstream is the direction from the CMTS to the CM, and upstream is the direction from the CM to the CMTS. The head-end is the origination point in most cable systems of the subscriber video signals and is generally also the location of the CMTS equipment. MAC Packet is a term referring to a DOCSIS Protocol Data Unit. RF refers to Radio Frequency. A SID refers to a DOCSIS Service ID, which identifies a particular upstream bandwidth allocation and class-of-service management for DOCSIS, and identifies a particular bidirectional security association for BPI. TLV stands for Type, Length, Value, an encoding method consisting of three fields: the first indicates the type of element, the second indicates the length, and the third contains the element's value.
sections.plainLanguage: The glossary sets out the cable vocabulary: the modem at the customer, the equipment at the head end that talks to it, and the direction each way.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Offering high speed internet service in the cable industry has become extremely successful, and DOCSIS devices are being deployed at a rate of multiple thousands per day. Operators are enjoying successful deployment but are also facing the challenge of properly managing deployed devices. Operators are using SNMP, the set of MIBs required by DOCSIS, and SNMP notifications to manage deployed DOCSIS devices. The use of SNMP notification for event reporting is becoming more popular as an effective and efficient method for network monitoring.

Unfortunately, only a minimal set of SNMP notifications was available. This notification MIB, together with the DOCSIS specifications, provides a minimum set of standard DOCSIS notifications that DOCSIS devices SHOULD support, to enable successful management of DOCSIS devices and networks.

The document defines a set of objects required for the event notification management of DOCSIS-compliant cable modems and cable modem termination systems. Appendix H of the DOCSIS 1.1 specification defines all DOCSIS 1.1 required events, and appendix D of the DOCSIS 2.0 specification does that for DOCSIS 2.0. The notifications specified in this document are used to notify these events via SNMP.
sections.plainLanguage: Operators were already managing cable modems with SNMP, but the set of alarms was tiny. This document fills the gap with a standard minimum set that every DOCSIS device should support.

sections.title: Structure of the MIB
sections.content:
The DOCS-IETF-CABLE-DEVICE-NOTIFICATION-MIB was designed to extend the RFC 2669 notification module.

Two groups of SNMP notification objects are defined. One group defines notifications for cable modem events, and the other group defines notifications for cable modem termination system events.

DOCSIS defines numerous events, and each event is assigned to a functional category. This MIB defines a notification object for each functional category. The varbinding list of each notification includes information about the event that occurred on the device.
sections.plainLanguage: One group of alarms for the modem, one for the head end. Each category of event gets its own alarm, and the alarm carries the details of what happened.

sections.title: The Control Objects and the Notifications
sections.content:
The module is registered under docsDevNotifMIB { mib-2 132 }, with docsDevNotifControl, docsDevCmNotifs and docsDevCmtsNotifs below it.

Two read-write objects switch the notifications on and off. docsDevCmNotifControl is a bit field with sixteen bits, one per cable modem notification: cmInitTLVUnknownNotif, cmDynServReqFailNotif, cmDynServRspFailNotif, cmDynServAckFailNotif, cmBpiInitNotif, cmBPKMNotif, cmDynamicSANotif, cmDHCPFailNotif, cmSwUpgradeInitNotif, cmSwUpgradeFailNotif, cmSwUpgradeSuccessNotif, cmSwUpgradeCVCNotif, cmTODFailNotif, cmDCCReqFailNotif, cmDCCRspFailNotif and cmDCCAckFailNotif. docsDevCmtsNotifControl is the same idea for the head end, with twelve bits: cmtsInitRegReqFailNotif, cmtsInitRegRspFailNotif, cmtsInitRegAckFailNotif, cmtsDynServReqFailNotif, cmtsDynServRspFailNotif, cmtsDynServAckFailNotif, cmtsBpiInitNotif, cmtsBPKMNotif, cmtsDynamicSANotif, cmtsDCCReqFailNotif, cmtsDCCRspFailNotif and cmtsDCCAckFailNotif. If the first bit is set then that notification is enabled; if it is not set the notification is disabled. Notifications are also under the control of the MIB modules defined in RFC 3413. If the device is rebooted, the value of these objects SHOULD revert to the default value, which is the empty set, so no notification is enabled until an operator asks for one.

Each notification carries the same core objects in its varbinding list. docsDevEvLevel is the priority level associated with the event, docsDevEvId is the unique identifier of the event that occurred, and docsDevEvText is a textual description of the event. For the cable modem group come ifPhysAddress, the MAC address of the cable interface of the modem, docsIfCmCmtsAddress, the MAC address of the CMTS the modem is connected to, docsIfDocsisBaseCapability, the highest version of the DOCSIS specification the device can support, docsIfCmStatusDocsisOperMode, the quality of service level the modem is operating in, and docsIfCmStatusModulationType, the upstream modulation methodology the modem uses. The software upgrade notifications add docsDevSwFilename and docsDevSwServer.

For the head end group the objects are the mirror image: docsIfCmtsCmStatusMacAddress is the MAC address of the modem the notification concerns, ifPhysAddress is the MAC address of the CMTS cable interface connected to that modem, docsIfCmtsCmStatusDocsisRegMode is the quality of service level the reporting modem is operating in, docsIfDocsisBaseCapability is again the highest DOCSIS version supported, and docsIfCmtsCmStatusModulationType is the upstream modulation methodology of the modem.
sections.plainLanguage: Two switches turn the alarms on and off, one for the modem side and one for the head end. Each alarm repeats the same handful of facts: how serious it was, what it was, and which device it happened on.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
There are two management objects defined in this MIB module with a MAX-ACCESS clause of read-write or read-create, docsDevCmNotifControl and docsDevCmtsNotifControl. Such objects may be considered sensitive or vulnerable in some network environments, and support for SET operations in a non-secure environment without proper protection can have a negative effect on network operations.

Setting either control object may cause flooding of notifications, which can disrupt network service. Besides causing flooding, changing the objects can also mean that notifications will not be emitted when one intends that to happen.

This MIB defines a number of notification objects that send detailed information about the event that caused the notification. Information in the notification message includes the event priority, the event id, the event message body, the modem's DOCSIS capability, its DOCSIS quality of service level, its DOCSIS upstream modulation type, the cable interface MAC address of the cable modem, and the cable card MAC address of the CMTS to which the modem is connected. Monitoring these notification messages could be used to gather information about the state of the network and the devices attached to it.

SNMP versions prior to SNMPv3 did not include adequate security. It is RECOMMENDED that implementers consider the security features provided by the SNMPv3 framework, including full support for the SNMPv3 cryptographic mechanisms for authentication and privacy, and that deployment of SNMP versions prior to SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED. It is then a customer or operator responsibility to ensure that the SNMP entity giving access to an instance of this MIB module is properly configured to give access to the objects only to those principals that have legitimate rights to read or change them.
sections.plainLanguage: The two switches are the sensitive part. An attacker who can write them can silence the alarms or set off a flood of them. The alarms themselves also reveal the state of the network, so SNMPv3 with encryption is recommended.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: The MIB module defined in this document uses the IANA-assigned OBJECT IDENTIFIER value docsDevNotifMIB { mib-2 132 }, recorded in the SMI Numbers registry.
sections.plainLanguage: The module is registered under the number 132 in the SMI Numbers registry.
